knowledge:
- key_parameters:
    - exposures.samCol: Column name identifying individuals in the exposures file (default is "sample").
    - phenotype.samCol: Column name identifying individuals in the phenotypes file (default is "sample").
    - description.expCol: Column name identifying exposures in the description file (default is "exposure").
    - description.famCol: Column name identifying exposure families in the description file (default is "family").
    - exposures.asFactor: Numeric threshold; exposures with fewer unique values than this are treated as categorical (default is 5).
    - method: In standardize(), the method used to scale continuous exposures ("normal", "robust", or "iqr").
    - pca: In pca(), a logical flag; if TRUE, performs a standard PCA instead of Factor Analysis of Mixed Data (FAMD).
    - family: In exwas() and mexwas(), the distribution family of the health outcome (e.g., "gaussian" for continuous, "binomial" for binary).
    - rid: In toES(), the index of the imputed dataset to extract from an imExposomeSet.
- alternatives:
    - mice or Hmisc: Used for missing data imputation. rexposome provides a wrapper imputation() using Hmisc internally, but recommends using mice for multiple imputation workflows, which are then loaded via loadImputed().
- when_to_use:
    - Use this package when you have a dataset containing multiple environmental/lifestyle exposures, subject phenotypes, and exposure metadata, and you want to perform systematic association studies (ExWAS) or multivariate variable selection.
- pitfalls:
    - Continuous exposures must follow a normal distribution for many downstream parametric tests; non-normal exposures should be transformed or inspected.
    - Categorical exposures must be correctly formatted as factors before running imputation or analysis.
    - The clustering() function will automatically discard non-continuous exposures and issue a warning.
    - When using loadExposome() with data.frames, the description data.frame must have the exposure names set as its rownames.

workflows.name: standard_exposome_analysis
workflows.intent: Load standard exposome data, pre-process it, explore relationships, and perform association studies (ExWAS, Inverse ExWAS, and Elastic Net).
workflows.stages: 1. Load data using readExposome or loadExposome ;; 2. Assess missingness and normality ;; 3. Impute missing values ;; 4. Standardize and perform PCA/FAMD ;; 5. Compute exposure correlations and cluster individuals ;; 6. Run univariate ExWAS, Inverse ExWAS, and multivariate mexwas.
workflows.code:
library(rexposome)
path <- file.path(path.package("rexposome"), "extdata")
description <- file.path(path, "description.csv")
phenotype <- file.path(path, "phenotypes.csv")
exposures <- file.path(path, "exposures.csv")
exp <- readExposome(exposures = exposures, description = description, phenotype = phenotype, exposures.samCol = "idnum", description.expCol = "Exposure", description.famCol = "Family", phenotype.samCol = "idnum")
tableMissings(exp, set = "exposures", output = "n")
tableMissings(exp, set = "phenotypes", output = "n")
plotMissings(exp, set = "exposures")
nm <- normalityTest(exp)
library(ggplot2)
plotHistogram(exp, select = "G_pesticides") + ggtitle("Garden Pesticides")
exp <- imputation(exp)
plotFamily(exp, family = "all")
exp_std <- standardize(exp, method = "normal")
exp_pca <- pca(exp_std, pca = TRUE)
plotPCA(exp_pca, set = "all")
plotPCA(exp_pca, set = "samples", phenotype = "sex")
plot3PCA(exp_pca, cmpX=1, cmpY=2, cmpZ=3, phenotype = "sex")
exp_cr <- correlation(exp, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method.cor = "pearson")
extract(exp_cr)[1:4, 1:4]
plotCorrelation(exp_cr, type = "circos")
hclust_data <- function(data, ...) { hclust(d = dist(x = data), ...) }
hclust_k3 <- function(result) { cutree(result, k = 3) }
exp_c <- clustering(exp, method = hclust_data, cmethod = hclust_k3)
plotClassification(exp_c)
plotEXP(exp_pca) + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6.5)) + ylab("")
plotPHE(exp_pca)
fl_ew <- exwas(exp, formula = blood_pre ~ sex + age, family = "gaussian")
we_ew <- exwas(exp, formula = wheezing ~ sex + age, family = "binomial")
head(extract(fl_ew))
clr <- rainbow(length(familyNames(exp)))
names(clr) <- familyNames(exp)
plotExwas(fl_ew, we_ew, color = clr) + ggtitle("Exposome Association Study - Univariate Approach")
plotEffect(fl_ew)
inv_ex <- invExWAS(exp, formula = ~flu + sex)
head(extract(inv_ex))
bl_mew <- mexwas(exp_std, phenotype = "blood_pre", family = "gaussian")
we_mew <- mexwas(exp_std, phenotype = "wheezing", family = "binomial")
plotExwas(bl_mew, we_mew) + ylab("") + ggtitle("Exposome Association Study - Multivariate Approach")

workflows.name: multiple_imputation_exposome
workflows.intent: Load multiple imputed exposome data, explore imputed families, extract single imputed sets, and perform ExWAS.
workflows.stages: 1. Load raw data and perform multiple imputation using mice ;; 2. Combine imputed datasets into a single data.frame ;; 3. Load the combined data into an imExposomeSet ;; 4. Visualize exposure behavior across imputations ;; 5. Extract a single ExposomeSet or run ExWAS directly on the imputed set.
workflows.code:
library(rexposome)
library(mice)
path <- file.path(path.package("rexposome"), "extdata")
description <- file.path(path, "description.csv")
phenotype <- file.path(path, "phenotypes.csv")
exposures <- file.path(path, "exposures.csv")
dd <- read.csv(description, header=TRUE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
ee <- read.csv(exposures, header=TRUE)
pp <- read.csv(phenotype, header=TRUE)
dd <- dd[-which(dd$Family %in% c("Phthalates", "PBDEs", "PFOAs", "Metals")), ]
ee <- ee[ , c("idnum", dd$Exposure)]
rownames(ee) <- ee$idnum
rownames(pp) <- pp$idnum
dta <- cbind(ee[ , -1], pp[ , -1])
for(ii in c(1:13, 18:47, 55:56)) { dta[, ii] <- as.numeric(dta[ , ii]) }
for(ii in c(14:17, 48:54)) { dta[ , ii] <- as.factor(dta[ , ii]) }
imp <- mice(dta[ , -52], pred = quickpred(dta[ , -52], mincor = 0.2, minpuc = 0.4), seed = 38788, m = 5, maxit = 10, printFlag = FALSE)
me <- complete(imp, action = 0)
me[ , ".imp"] <- 0
me[ , ".id"] <- rownames(me)
for(set in 1:5) {
    im <- complete(imp, action = set)
    im[ , ".imp"] <- set
    im[ , ".id"] <- rownames(im)
    me <- rbind(me, im)
}
me <- me[ , c(".imp", ".id", setdiff(colnames(me), c(".imp", ".id")))]
rownames(me) <- 1:nrow(me)
ex_imp <- loadImputed(data = me, description = dd, description.famCol = "Family", description.expCol = "Exposure")
plotFamily(ex_imp, family = "Organochlorines")
ex_1 <- toES(ex_imp, rid = 1)
as_iew <- exwas(ex_imp, formula = blood_pre~sex+age, family = "gaussian")
clr <- rainbow(length(familyNames(ex_imp)))
names(clr) <- familyNames(ex_imp)
plotExwas(as_iew, color = clr)
thr <- tef(as_iew)
tbl <- extract(as_iew)
sig <- tbl[tbl$pvalue <= thr, ]
